gaps.sentence: 'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'The flight leaves now,' the announcer said. The announcer said that the flight left ___.
gaps.explanation: Now becomes then in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
gaps.explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll definitely pay you back,' he said. He ___ to pay me back.
gaps.explanation: Promises take promise + to-infinitive: promised to pay me back.

gaps.sentence: 'Stop the car!' the passenger shouted. The passenger shouted at the driver ___ the car.
gaps.hint: shout at sb to do sth
gaps.explanation: The command is reported with shout at + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Watch out for the ice on the road,' she said. She ___ us about the icy road.
gaps.explanation: Warnings about a danger: warn somebody about something (or warn sb to do).
